scenario: Two wildfire drone-mapping systems, DroneX and DroneY, are evaluated on successful area-mapping rates across steep and flat terrain bands. DroneX is predominantly deployed in challenging steep terrain; DroneY mostly operates in flat terrain.

data.description: Successful mapping completion rates by terrain band

question: (a) Which system has the higher aggregate mapping rate? (b) Which performs better within each terrain band? (c) Compute corrected rates assuming a 50/50 terrain mix.

ground_truth.explanation: DroneY's better aggregate is caused by its easy flat-terrain workload. Standardising to 50/50 terrain reveals DroneX is superior in both strata.

naive_answer: DroneY is better; aggregate rate 0.8857 vs DroneX's 0.8186.
naive_trap: Terrain band confounds performance; DroneX handles 85.7% steep missions while DroneY handles 85.7% flat ones.
reasoning_trace: Steep: X 0.80 > Y 0.74. Flat: X 0.93 > Y 0.91. Corrected: X=0.865, Y=0.825. X wins.
python_verification:
nD1s,rD1s,nD1f,rD1f = 600,0.80,100,0.93
nD2s,rD2s,nD2f,rD2f = 100,0.74,600,0.91
ovD1=(nD1s*rD1s+nD1f*rD1f)/(nD1s+nD1f); ovD2=(nD2s*rD2s+nD2f*rD2f)/(nD2s+nD2f)
assert ovD2 > ovD1
cD1=0.5*rD1s+0.5*rD1f; cD2=0.5*rD2s+0.5*rD2f
assert abs(cD1-0.865)<0.005 and abs(cD2-0.825)<0.005
assert cD1 > cD2
